title: Twisting commutes with completed derived scalar extension
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $E\subset F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $R_E,R_F$ be the completed coefficient sheaves of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let $m\in\mathbf Z$. Let $D^b_c(S,\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived-complete integral category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Let $L_E=\mathcal O_E(m)$ and $L_F=\mathcal O_F(m)$ be the twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], identified after base change by the canonical isomorphism of [lem-weil-integral-twist-base-change]. For every derived-complete $C\in D^b_c(S,\mathcal O_E)$ and a K-flat resolution with flat terms $P\to C$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the termwise map $$ (P\otimes_{R_E}L_E)\otimes_{R_E}R_F\longrightarrow(P\otimes_{R_E}R_F)\otimes_{R_F}L_F,\qquad (x\otimes l)\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes b)\otimes(l\otimes1), $$ is a chain isomorphism. Writing $\operatorname{Ext}_{F/E}$ for the completed integral scalar-extension functor of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], this chain map, conjugated by the natural ordinary-to-completed comparison of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], induces a natural isomorphism $$\operatorname{Ext}_{F/E}(C(m))\cong\operatorname{Ext}_{F/E}(C)(m)$$ in the completed integral categories.

proof.text: Write $R=R_E$, $B=R_F$, $L=L_E$, and let $\theta:L\otimes_R B\xrightarrow{\sim}L_F$ be [lem-weil-integral-twist-base-change]. For $H=E,F$, clause 3 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] trivializes $\mathcal O_H(1)$ over $R_H$ and identifies its finite reductions with finite locally constant rank-one lines. By [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], positive twists are tensor powers, the zero twist is $R_H$, and negative twists are sheaf duals. Restriction of tensor is [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction], and [def-pur-sheaf-hom] computes the dual on the localized site. Thus on a first-line trivializing cover every $L_H$ and its dual are $R_H$. Evaluation $L_H\otimes L_H^\vee\to R_H$ and the reverse-order evaluation are locally multiplication and hence are global isomorphisms: their local inverses agree because an inverse is unique, and glue by the sheaf axiom. Reduction of these same formulas identifies $L_H\otimes_{R_H}(A_{H,n})_S$ with $A_{H,n}(m)$ for all $n$: tensor powers reduce by balancing, while a dual basis reduces to the dual basis. These reductions are finite locally constant rank-one sheaves, including for $m=0$ and $m<0$.

proof.text: For either $H$, tensoring with $L_H$ and $L_H^\vee$ gives inverse additive equivalences, by the associativity and unit maps of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] and the evaluations in step 1. These functors preserve kernels and cokernels: applying the inverse equivalence identifies maps into a proposed kernel (or out of a proposed cokernel) with the corresponding universal problem before tensoring. Hence $T_H=-\otimes_{R_H}L_H$ and its inverse are exact. In particular $L_H$ and $L_H^\vee$ are flat by [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The cohomology formula of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] gives $\mathcal H^i(T_H Q)\cong T_H\mathcal H^i(Q)$ for every complex $Q$. Since the inverse equivalence detects zero objects, this preserves precisely each cohomological vanishing interval.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product); exact inverse tensor equivalences and kernel/image computation

proof.text: Choose the given $P\to C$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The complex $L[0]$ is K-flat: tensoring any acyclic complex with it is its image under the exact $T_E$, acyclic by step 2 and [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The same holds for $L_F[0]$. Moreover $P\otimes_R L$ is K-flat with flat terms. Its term $P^i\otimes_R L$ is flat since tensoring by it is the composite of two exact tensor functors. For an acyclic $Q$, associativity gives $Q\otimes_R(P\otimes_R L)\cong(Q\otimes_R P)\otimes_R L$, acyclic by K-flatness of $P$ and exactness of $T_E$. Here total tensor uses [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Rebracketing its direct sums is valid because the closed tensor adjunction in [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] makes $-\otimes_R L$ preserve them: maps from the tensor of a sum correspond to the product of the maps from the tensor of each summand. Since $L$ is concentrated in degree zero, rebracketing changes no differential signs. These arguments apply over $B$ as well.

Before using $\theta$, define
$$u:(P\otimes_R L)\otimes_R B\longrightarrow(P\otimes_R B)\otimes_B(L\otimes_R B),\qquad (x\otimes l)\otimes b\longmapsto(x\otimes b)\otimes(l\otimes1).$$
Its inverse sends $(x\otimes b)\otimes(l\otimes c)$ to $(x\otimes l)\otimes bc$. Both formulas are additive and $R$-balanced in $x,l$; moving a $B$-scalar between the two right-hand factors does not change $bc$. The universal properties of [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] and [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension] therefore extend these formulas to morphisms of the sheaf tensors, commuting with restriction. Their composites are identities: on the left the scalar becomes $b\cdot1$; on the right move $c$ from $l\otimes c=c(l\otimes1)$ into $x\otimes b$. Equality on these pure inputs determines sheaf maps by those same universal properties; no assertion that all global sections are pure tensors is needed. Composing $u$ with $1\otimes\theta$ gives exactly the map in the statement. Its inverse is the displayed inverse after $1\otimes\theta^{-1}$. Only $x$ has nonzero complex degree, so both maps commute with $d_P$ and are inverse chain maps. This proves the chain-isomorphism clause.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), tensor formulas and bilinear universal property

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], the K-flat flat-term complexes from step 3 compute $C(m)=C\otimes_R^L L$. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], the source of the chain map in step 4 computes $(C(m))\otimes_R^L B$. On the other side [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] makes $P\otimes_R B$ K-flat with flat terms over $B$; together with $L_F[0]$ this computes $(C\otimes_R^L B)\otimes_B^L L_F$. Thus step 4 induces an isomorphism
$$\alpha_C:(C(m))\otimes_R^L B\xrightarrow{\sim}(C\otimes_R^L B)(m).$$
For a chain map $f:P\to P'$, the two naturality paths on a pure input both give $(f(x)\otimes b)\otimes\theta(l\otimes1)$. The localization equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] extends this naturality from K-flat models, including inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, to all derived morphisms. The change-of-rings comparison is independent of the resolution by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Therefore $\alpha$ is natural in $C$ and independent of the chosen $P$.

Let $H$ be either coefficient field and let $K$ be derived complete over $R_H$. Step 1 verifies the locally free rank-one hypothesis of [lem-sf-integral-line-tensor-comparison], so its canonical map identifies $K\otimes_{R_H}^L L_H$ with the derived limit of the tensor/reduction tower. Its statement specifies that the map is induced by the natural reduction maps, with the ordinary tensor/reduction comparison at every level. On a K-flat model this comparison sends $(x\otimes l)\otimes a$ to $(x\otimes a)\otimes(l\otimes1)$, precisely step 4 with $B=(A_{H,n})_S$. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] these level complexes compute the reductions of $K(m)$. Their quotient transitions and maps from $K(m)$ agree on the displayed inputs. Consequently the Roos triangle supplied by that comparison has first map equal to the reduction map $K(m)\to\prod_n K(m)_n$, as required in [def-weil-derived-complete]. Thus $K(m)$ is derived complete. This uses the specified natural comparison, without choosing a lift into an arbitrary triangulated derived limit.

source.place: Definition 3.4.10, Lemma 3.4.12(4), Definition 3.5.2; existing integral line tensor comparison specialized to L_H

proof.text: If $K\in D^b_c(S,\mathcal O_H)$, [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] gives one interval $[r,s]$ for all its constructible reductions $K_n$. Steps 4-5 with the quotient ring identify $(K(m))_n$ with $K_n\otimes^L_{(A_{H,n})_S}A_{H,n}(m)$. The finite line is flat and its tensor is exact by the inverse-line argument of step 2. The cohomology comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] therefore identifies its cohomology with $\mathcal H^i(K_n)\otimes A_{H,n}(m)$ and preserves $[r,s]$. To check constructibility, choose the finite partition for each $\mathcal H^i(K_n)$ in [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. On each stratum the tensor restricts to the tensor of restrictions by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. Refine the local constant cover of the original sheaf with that of the finite line from step 1. There its tensor is $M\otimes A_{H,n}\cong M$ with $M$ finite. Thus the same finite partition is a constructible partition for the tensor. Step 6 supplies completeness, so the definition gives $K(m)\in D^b_c(S,\mathcal O_H)$. There is no assertion about a finite global trivializing cover or about a discrete integral coefficient sheaf.

Both $C$ and $C(m)$ are derived complete by the hypothesis and step 6. Apply [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] to them to obtain the specified natural isomorphisms $\chi_C:C\otimes_R^L B\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Ext}_{F/E}C$ and $\chi_{C(m)}:(C(m))\otimes_R^L B\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Ext}_{F/E}(C(m))$. With the notation of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], set
$$\beta_C=(\chi_C)(m)\circ\alpha_C\circ\chi_{C(m)}^{-1}.$$
Every factor is an isomorphism; each is natural, so their composite is natural. This is exactly the stated chain map conjugated by the specified ordinary-to-completed comparisons. By [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible] and step 7, the source and target of $\beta_C$ lie in $D^b_c(S,\mathcal O_F)$. Since this is a full subcategory, the ambient isomorphism is the asserted isomorphism in the completed integral category. The comparison lemma also makes ordinary scalar extension derived complete, so all intermediate twists used above have their claimed complete interpretation.
